# 1 Maccabees Chapter 14 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 14 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 14 is the literary and theological high point of 1 Maccabees. Verses 4–15 constitute an embedded encomium (praise-poem) in heightened, parallelistic prose modeled on biblical poetry — particularly the idealized descriptions of Solomon's reign and prophetic visions of future peace (cf. Zech 3:10, Mic 4:4). The poem must be formatted as verse. The inscription (vv.27-45) is a formal legal document and must be rendered with precision.

**Key term rulings:**
- Verses 4b-15 formatted as poetry (indented parallelistic lines) across all agents
- "vine and fig tree" (v.12) — preserved literally; deliberately echoes Mic 4:4 and 1 Kgs 4:25
- "old men sat in the streets" (v.9) — echoes Zech 8:4; preserved
- "ethnarch" (v.46) — Greek ἐθνάρχης; preserved as transliteration; a new political title
- "faithful prophet" (v.41) — the caveat "until a trustworthy prophet should arise" is a major theological statement implying the Hasmoneans' authority lacks full prophetic legitimacy
- "Friend of Kings" appears in v.38 indirectly through Demetrius's confirmation
- "gold ornament" / "gold buckle" (v.43-44) — SOPHIA: "gold ornament" in v.43, "gold clasp" in v.44 for consistency

---

**1** In the one hundred and seventy-second year King Demetrius assembled his forces and marched into Media to gather auxiliary forces to fight against Trypho.

**2** When Arsaces king of Persia and Media heard that Demetrius had entered his territories, he sent one of his commanders to take him alive.

**3** The commander marched out, defeated the army of Demetrius, captured him, and brought him to Arsaces, who kept him under guard.

**4** The land of Judea was at rest all the days of Simon. He sought the welfare of his nation, and his authority and glory pleased them all his days.

---

*[Verses 5–15: An encomium in praise of Simon, composed in heightened parallelistic prose.]*

**5** Among his glorious deeds was this: he took Joppa as a harbor
    and made a way to the islands of the sea.

**6** He enlarged the borders of his nation
    and gained mastery over the land.

**7** He gathered many captives
    and held dominion over Gazara and Beth-zur and the citadel;
    he removed its uncleannesses from it,
    and there was no one who resisted him.

**8** They tilled their land in peace,
    and the land gave its produce,
    and the trees of the plain gave their fruit.

**9** Old men sat in the streets,
    speaking together about good things,
    and the young men put on glorious and warlike apparel.

**10** He provided food for the cities
    and furnished them with the means of defense,
    until his glorious name was known to the ends of the earth.

**11** He made peace in the land,
    and Israel rejoiced with great joy.

**12** Every man sat under his vine
    and under his fig tree,
    and there was no one to make them afraid.

**13** No enemy remained in the land to fight against them,
    and the kings were crushed in those days.

**14** He strengthened all the humble of his people;
    he sought out the law
    and removed every lawless and wicked person.

**15** He made the sanctuary glorious
    and multiplied the sacred vessels.

---

**16** When news reached Rome and Sparta that Jonathan had died, they were deeply grieved.

**17** But when they heard that his brother Simon had become high priest in his place and was governing the country and its cities,

**18** they wrote to him on bronze tablets to renew the friendship and alliance that they had established with his brothers Judas and Jonathan.

**19** These were read before the assembly in Jerusalem.

**20** This is a copy of the letter that the Spartans sent: "The rulers and the city of the Spartans to Simon the great priest and to the elders and priests and the rest of the Jewish people, our brothers, greetings.

**21** The envoys who were sent to our people reported to us about your glory and honor, and we were glad at their coming.

**22** What they said we have recorded in the decrees of the people as follows: Numenius son of Antiochus and Antipater son of Jason, envoys of the Jews, came to us to renew our friendship.

**23** The people resolved to receive these men with honor and to place a copy of their address in the public archives, so that the Spartan people might have a record of it. And a copy of this has been sent to Simon the great priest."

**24** After this Simon sent Numenius to Rome with a large golden shield weighing a thousand minas, to confirm the alliance with the Romans.

**25** When the people heard these things, they said: "What thanks shall we give to Simon and his sons?

**26** For he and his brothers and his father's house have stood firm, repulsed Israel's enemies, and secured their freedom." They wrote this on bronze tablets and set them up on pillars on Mount Zion.

**27** This is a copy of the inscription: "On the eighteenth day of Elul, in the one hundred and seventy-second year — which is the third year of Simon the great high priest —

**28** in Asaramel, in a great assembly of priests and people and rulers of the nation and elders of the country, it was made known as follows:

**29** Since wars have often occurred in our land, Simon son of Mattathias, a priest of the family of Joarib, and his brothers exposed themselves to danger and resisted the enemies of their nation, in order that their sanctuary and the law might be maintained; and they glorified their nation with great glory.

**30** Jonathan rallied the nation, became their high priest, and was gathered to his people.

**31** Their enemies then sought to invade their land and lay hands on their sanctuary.

**32** Then Simon rose up and fought for his nation and spent much of his own money; he armed the warriors of his nation and paid their wages.

**33** He fortified the cities of Judea and Beth-zur on the border of Judea, where formerly the weapons of the enemy had been stored, and he stationed a garrison of Jewish men there.

**34** He also fortified Joppa which is by the sea, and Gazara on the borders of Azotus, where the enemy had previously been established, and he settled Jews there and provided whatever was needed for the restoration of these cities.

**35** The people saw Simon's faithfulness and the glory he sought to bring to his nation, and made him their leader and high priest — because of all these things, and because of the righteousness and faithfulness he had maintained toward his nation, and because he sought in every way to exalt his people.

**36** In his days things prospered under his hand: the Gentiles were removed from their land, as were those in the city of David in Jerusalem, who had built themselves a citadel from which they would go out to defile the precincts of the sanctuary, causing great harm to its purity.

**37** He settled Jews in it and fortified it for the security of the land and of the city, and he raised the walls of Jerusalem higher.

**38** On account of these things, King Demetrius confirmed him in the high priesthood,

**39** made him one of his friends, and honored him with great honor.

**40** For he had heard that the Romans had proclaimed the Jews friends and allies and brothers, and had received the envoys of Simon with honor.

**41** The Jews and their priests decreed that Simon should be their leader and high priest in perpetuity, until a faithful prophet should arise,

**42** and that he should be their military commander and take charge of the sanctuary, and appoint officials over the public works and over the country and over the arms and the strongholds;

**43** and that he should take charge of the sanctuary; and that all public contracts in the country should be written in his name; and that he should be clothed in purple and wear a gold ornament.

**44** It shall not be lawful for any of the people or the priests to annul any of these decrees or to contradict his orders, or to convene any assembly in the country without him, or to be clothed in purple or to wear a gold clasp.

**45** Whoever acts contrary to these decrees or contravenes any of them shall be liable to punishment.

**46** All the people approved the ordaining of these things for Simon. Simon accepted them and was pleased to serve as high priest, commander, and ethnarch of the Jews and priests, and to be the protector of all.

**47** They gave orders that this inscription should be placed on bronze tablets and set up in the precinct of the sanctuary in a conspicuous place,

**48** and that copies should be deposited in the treasury, so that Simon and his sons might have them.
